
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import duckdb

from datetime import datetime
import re
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')  # Suppress all warnings

path_delivered_fuels =  "/workspaces/reports/data/fuel_costs/propane/eia_weekly_heatingoil_propane_prices_MA_20250411.xls"
delivered_fuels = pd.read_excel(path_delivered_fuels, sheet_name="Data 1", skiprows=2)

# Split the Date column into year, month, day
delivered_fuels['year'] = pd.to_datetime(delivered_fuels['Date']).dt.year.astype(int)
delivered_fuels['month'] = pd.to_datetime(delivered_fuels['Date']).dt.month.astype(int)
delivered_fuels['day'] = pd.to_datetime(delivered_fuels['Date']).dt.day.astype(int)

print([col for col in delivered_fuels.columns])

# Propane: 27kWh per gallon (https://www.propane101.com/propanevselectricity.htm)
delivered_fuels['propane_dollars_per_kwh'] = delivered_fuels['Weekly Massachusetts Propane Residential Price  (Dollars per Gallon)'] / 27

# Fuel Oil: 145.945 MJ per gallon (https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/units-and-calculators/energy-conversion-calculators.php)
# 40.2778 kWh/gallon
delivered_fuels['fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh'] = delivered_fuels['Weekly Massachusetts No. 2 Heating Oil Residential Price  (Dollars per Gallon)'] / 40.2778

# Group by year and month and calculate mean prices
delivered_fuels_monthly = delivered_fuels.groupby(['year', 'month']).agg({
    'propane_dollars_per_kwh': 'mean',
    'fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh': 'mean'
}).reset_index()



# PROPANE
propane_supply_rates = delivered_fuels_monthly[['year', 'month', 'propane_dollars_per_kwh']]
propane_supply_rates.to_csv("/workspaces/reports/data/fuel_costs/propane/ma_propane_supply_rates.csv", index=False)

# Write to database
# con = duckdb.connect('/workspaces/reports/data/ResStock/2022_resstock_amy2018_release_1.1/rs_ma_hp_rates_2.db')
# con.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS supply_rates_propane")
# con.execute("CREATE TABLE supply_rates_propane AS SELECT * FROM propane_supply_rates")
# con.close()

# FUEL OIL
fuel_oil_supply_rates = delivered_fuels_monthly[['year', 'month', 'fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh']]
fuel_oil_supply_rates.to_csv("/workspaces/reports/data/fuel_costs/fuel_oil/ma_fuel_oil_supply_rates.csv", index=False)
```

```{python}
import plotly.express as px

# Create datetime column with first day of each month
# Drop unnecessary columns
delivered_fuels_monthly = delivered_fuels.drop(['Weekly Massachusetts No. 2 Heating Oil Wholesale/Resale Price  (Dollars per Gallon)', 'day', 'Date'], axis=1)

delivered_fuels_monthly['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(
    delivered_fuels_monthly[['year', 'month']].assign(day=1),
    format='%Y-%m-%d'
)

# Create figure with both lines
fig = px.line(delivered_fuels_monthly,
              x='Date',
              y=['propane_dollars_per_kwh', 'fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh'],
              title='Delivered Fuel Prices Over Time',
              labels={
                  'value': 'Price ($/kWh)',
                  'variable': 'Fuel Type',
                  'Date': 'Date'
              })

# Update the legend labels to be more readable
fig.update_traces(
    name='Propane',
    selector=dict(name='propane_dollars_per_kwh')
)
fig.update_traces(
    name='Fuel Oil',
    selector=dict(name='fuel_oil_dollars_per_kwh')
)

# Customize layout
fig.update_layout(
    showlegend=True,
    hovermode='x unified',
    yaxis_title='Price ($/kWh)'
)

fig.show()

```
